props.title: The World's Largest Engineering Competition
body: Formula Student challenges university teams to design, build, and compete with a single-seat race car, judged across engineering, business, and performance criteria.

Founded in 1981 in the United States as Formula SAE, the competition has grown to include events on every continent. Each year, hundreds of university teams go head-to-head, proving their engineering prowess on and off the track.

The competition is not about building the fastest car - it's about building the best overall package. Teams must demonstrate excellence in engineering design, cost planning, business presentation, and on-track performance.

props.label: Judged Off-Track
props.title: Static Events (325 Points)
props.intro: Before hitting the track, teams present their engineering decisions, business plan, and cost analysis to industry judges.

cards.title: Engineering Design
cards.subtitle: 150 Points
cards.text: Teams present and defend their technical design choices to a panel of experienced industry engineers. Judges evaluate innovation, engineering process, and understanding of vehicle dynamics.

cards.title: Cost & Manufacturing
cards.subtitle: 100 Points
cards.text: A detailed cost report covers every component. Teams demonstrate efficient manufacturing planning and show awareness of real-world production constraints and cost optimization.

cards.title: Business Presentation
cards.subtitle: 75 Points
cards.text: Teams pitch a business case to "investors" - presenting their car as a viable product. This tests communication, market analysis, and business strategy skills.

props.label: On-Track Performance
props.title: Dynamic Events (675 Points)
props.intro: The majority of points are earned on the track, testing every aspect of the car's performance.

events.title: Acceleration
events.text: A straight-line sprint of 75 metres from a standing start. Tests raw engine power, traction, and launch strategy. Top teams complete it under 4 seconds.

events.title: Skidpad
events.text: A figure-eight course testing lateral grip and cornering ability. Cars must navigate constant-radius turns, revealing suspension setup and tyre performance.

events.title: Autocross
events.text: A single-lap time attack on a technical circuit with tight corners, slaloms, and straights. Tests overall car balance and driver skill. Sets the starting order for endurance.

events.title: Endurance
events.text: The ultimate test: 22 kilometres of racing with a mandatory driver change. Tests reliability, consistency, and thermal management under sustained load. Worth the most points.

events.title: Energy Efficiency
events.text: Measured during the endurance event, this rewards teams who achieve peak performance with minimal energy consumption. Engineering efficiency at its finest.

props.label: Total: 1000 Points
props.title: Scoring Breakdown
props.outro: The best overall package wins. A car that excels in design and efficiency can beat a faster car that lacks engineering depth.

cards.title: Formula Student France (Transpolis)
cards.text: Our home competition, held annually at a circuit in France. This is our primary target for the 2025/2026 season. Teams from across Europe compete here.

cards.title: Formula Student Germany
cards.text: The largest and most prestigious FS event, held at Hockenheimring. A future goal as we grow and develop our car and team.

cards.title: Formula Student UK
cards.text: Held at Silverstone, one of the oldest and most respected events. An aspirational target for our second or third season.
